questions.question: Which body recommends the distribution of tax revenues between union and states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Finance Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Finance Commission** is a **constitutional body** established under **Article 280** of the **Constitution of India** to define the financial relations between the central government and the individual state governments.
 
• It is constituted by the **President of India** every **five years** or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary to ensure fiscal stability and **cooperative federalism**.
 
• The primary mandate of the commission is to recommend the **distribution of net proceeds of taxes** between the **Union** and the **States**, commonly referred to as **vertical devolution**.
 
• It also determines the allocation of these tax proceeds among the states themselves, known as **horizontal devolution**, based on various criteria like **fiscal capacity** and **demographic performance**.
 
• The commission specifies the principles that govern **Grants-in-aid** to the states out of the **Consolidated Fund of India** as per **Article 275**.
 
• Its recommendations are **advisory** in nature and are laid before both Houses of **Parliament** by the **President** under **Article 281**.
 
• The **15th Finance Commission**, chaired by **N.K. Singh**, recommended that the states be given **41%** of the divisible pool of central taxes for the period **2021-2026**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NITI Aayog**

 
 
• Established on **January 1, 2015**, it replaced the **Planning Commission** as the premier **policy think tank** of the Government of India.
 
• It provides directional and policy inputs while fostering **cooperative federalism** through a **bottom-up approach**.
 
 
 
• **Planning Commission**
 
 
• Formed in **1950** as a **non-constitutional** and **non-statutory** body to formulate India's **Five-Year Plans**.
 
• It was dissolved in **2014** to make way for a more contemporary and collaborative institution.
 
 
 
• **Parliament**
 
 
• The supreme **legislative body** of India, governed by **Articles 79 to 122** of the Constitution.
 
• While it approves the **Union Budget** and tax laws, it relies on the **Finance Commission** for professional recommendations on tax revenue sharing.

questions.question: Why is the Raga Tarangini considered highly important in Hindustani music history?

options.text: It uses many raga names still in use today

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It uses many raga names still in use today**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Raga Tarangini** is a monumental work in the history of **Indian classical music**, authored by **Pandit Lochana** (also known as **Lochan Kavi**), who hailed from the **Mithila** region.
 
• The text is believed to have been composed around the **15th century** (specifically dated by many scholars to **1460 AD**), serving as a crucial bridge between the ancient **Gram-Murchana** system and the modern **Thaat** or **Mela** system.
 
• Its primary importance lies in its nomenclature; it mentions and describes various **ragas** such as **Bhairavi**, **Todi**, **Kafi**, **Kalyan**, **Sarang**, and **Kanada**, which are still the backbone of modern **Hindustani music**.
 
• **Pandit Lochana** introduced a classification system based on **12 Melas** (parent scales), which simplified the complex theoretical frameworks of earlier texts like the **Sangeet Ratnakara**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lochan Kavi's Contribution**:

 
 
• His **12-Mela** system acted as a precursor to the **10-Thaat** classification system later standardized by **Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande** in the **20th century**.
 
• The work emphasizes the practical application of music, moving away from purely abstract ancient theories to reflect the actual performance practices of his time.
 
 
 
• **Context of Other Options**:
 
 
• **Harmonium and Tabla**: The **Harmonium** is a relatively modern instrument introduced to India in the **19th century** by **European** traders. While the **Tabla** is older, **Raga Tarangini** focuses on **Melodic theory** (Raga) rather than the introduction of these specific instruments.
 
• **Southern Ragas**: Although it shares the concept of **Melas** with **Carnatic music**, the text is fundamentally a pillar of **North Indian** or **Hindustani** musical evolution.
 
• **Traditional Theories**: Rather than rejecting traditional theories, the text **evolved** them to better suit the changing musical landscape of the medieval period.

questions.question: Which poetic collection by Sumitranandan Pant won him the Jnanpith Award?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chidambara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sumitranandan Pant** was honored with the prestigious **Jnanpith Award** in the year **1968** for his poetic collection titled **Chidambara**.
 
• He was the **first Hindi poet** to receive the **Jnanpith Award**, which is India's highest literary honor, establishing a landmark in Hindi literature.
 
• **Chidambara** is a compilation of his selected poems that reflect his transition from the **Chhayavaadi** (Romantic) style to a more philosophical and **humanistic** approach influenced by the teachings of **Sri Aurobindo**.
 
• The work is highly acclaimed for its rhythmic structure, aesthetic sensibility, and the profound exploration of the **universal consciousness** and human spirit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sumitranandan Pant**:

 
 
• Born in **Kausani**, Uttarakhand, he is famously known as the **Prakriti ke Sukumar Kavi** (Nature's Delicate Poet).
 
• He was one of the four main pillars of the **Chhayavaad** school of Hindi poetry.
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Bhushan** in **1961** and the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1960**.
 
 
 
• **Pallav**:
 
 
• Published in **1928**, it is considered one of the defining works of the **Chhayavaad** era, featuring a famous preface on Hindi poetics.
 
 
 
• **Kala Aur Budhdha Chand**:
 
 
• This collection earned him the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1960**, showcasing his mastery over modern poetic forms.
 
 
 
• **Veena**:
 
 
• One of his earliest works published in **1927**, primarily focusing on the raw beauty of **nature** and romantic themes.

questions.question: The Sunderbans Delta is formed by the confluence of which rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ganga and Brahmaputra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sunderbans Delta**, also known as the **Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta**, is the largest river delta in the world, located in the **South Asia** region.
 
• It is formed by the combined waters of the **Ganga** (Ganges) and **Brahmaputra** rivers, which empty into the **Bay of Bengal** after flowing through **India** and **Bangladesh**.
 
• The delta is a complex network of **distributaries**, islands, and **tidal waterways**, covering approximately 10,000 square kilometers of land and water.
 
• It is famously known for its vast **mangrove forests**, which act as a natural barrier against **cyclones** and storm surges from the ocean.
 
• The region is exceptionally fertile due to the continuous deposition of **alluvial soil** carried by the major river systems from the **Himalayas**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Flora and Fauna:**

 
 
• The delta is named after the **Sundari tree** (Heritiera fomes), which is the most dominant mangrove species in the area.
 
• It is the primary habitat for the **Royal Bengal Tiger**, known for its unique ability to swim in saline water.
 
 
 
• **International Recognition:**
 
 
• The **Sunderbans National Park** in India was designated a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in 1987.
 
• The entire area is recognized as a **Ramsar Site**, marking its status as a wetland of international importance.
 
 
 
• **River Systems:**
 
 
• While the **Ganga** and **Brahmaputra** are the primary architects, the **Meghna River** also merges with them in Bangladesh to form the final discharge.
 
• In contrast, the **Godavari and Krishna** rivers form a delta on the eastern coast of **Andhra Pradesh**, while the **Mahanadi** forms its delta in **Odisha**.

questions.question: The Himalayas are wider in which sector of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Western Himalayas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Himalayan mountain range** exhibits a significant variation in its width from west to east, stretching across an arc of approximately **2,400 km**.
 
• The **Western Himalayas**, which include the regions of **Jammu and Kashmir**, **Ladakh**, and parts of **Himachal Pradesh**, constitute the widest sector of the entire mountain system.
 
• In this western sector, the width of the mountains reaches approximately **400 km to 500 km**, providing a broad geographical expanse for various sub-ranges like the **Karakoram**, **Ladakh**, and **Zanskar**.
 
• In stark contrast, the **Eastern Himalayas**, primarily located in **Arunachal Pradesh**, narrow down considerably to a width of about **150 km**.
 
• The variation in width is geologically linked to the intensity of the **tectonic compression** between the **Indian Plate** and the **Eurasian Plate**; the compression was more intense in the east, resulting in a narrower but steeper mountain profile.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Himalayas**:

 
 
• This sector lies between the **Kali River** in the west and the **Teesta River** in the east, primarily covering the territory of **Nepal**.
 
• It serves as a transitional zone in terms of width and contains the highest peaks in the world, including **Mount Everest**.
 
 
 
• **Shiwalik Himalayas**:
 
 
• Also known as the **Outer Himalayas**, this is the southernmost and youngest range of the Himalayan system.
 
• Their width is quite small compared to the overall sector, ranging only from **10 km to 50 km**, with altitudes rarely exceeding **1,500 meters**.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Himalayas**:
 
 
• This region receives the highest **monsoonal rainfall**, leading to dense forest cover and high biodiversity.
 
• The abrupt rise from the **Brahmaputra plains** to high peaks is a hallmark of this narrower eastern sector.

questions.question: Who won the ICC Men's ODI Cricketer of the Year award in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Virat Kohli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Virat Kohli** was named the **ICC Men's ODI Cricketer of the Year** for **2023**, marking his fourth win in this category (previously in 2012, 2017, and 2018), which is the most by any player.
 
• He had an exceptional year in **One Day Internationals**, scoring a total of **1,377 runs** in 27 matches at a remarkable average of **72.47** and a strike rate of **99.13**.
 
• During the **2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup** hosted by India, Kohli broke the record for the most runs in a single edition of the tournament, amassing **765 runs** in 11 innings.
 
• He reached a historic milestone during the World Cup semi-final against **New Zealand** by scoring his **50th ODI century**, surpassing the legendary **Sachin Tendulkar's** record of 49 centuries.
 
• His consistent performance throughout the year included **six centuries** and eight half-centuries, helping India reach the finals of the **ODI World Cup** and win the **Asia Cup 2023**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other major **ICC Award** winners for 2023 include:

 
 
• **Pat Cummins**: The Australian skipper won the **Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy** for **ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year** after leading his team to the **WTC title** and **World Cup** glory.
 
• **Usman Khawaja**: Named the **ICC Men's Test Cricketer of the Year** for his prolific run-scoring at the top of the order for Australia.
 
• **Suryakumar Yadav**: Won the **ICC Men's T20I Cricketer of the Year** for the second consecutive year due to his innovative batting and high strike rate.
 
• **Rachin Ravindra**: The New Zealand all-rounder was named the **ICC Men's Emerging Cricketer of the Year**.

questions.question: How many key variables are used to rank countries in the Happiness Index?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Happiness Report** uses **six key variables** to measure and explain the variation of self-reported happiness across different nations globally.
 
• **GDP per Capita**: This variable represents the **economic power** of a country and is adjusted for **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** to reflect the relative living standards of its citizens.
 
• **Social Support**: This is measured by the national average of binary responses to the **Gallup World Poll** question asking if individuals have relatives or friends they can count on in times of trouble.
 
• **Healthy Life Expectancy**: This metric is derived from **World Health Organization (WHO)** data, estimating the number of years a person is expected to live in **full health**.
 
• **Freedom to Make Life Choices**: This captures the **individual autonomy** within a society, based on survey responses regarding satisfaction with the freedom to choose what to do with one's life.
 
• **Generosity**: This is calculated by comparing the average of responses on whether individuals have **donated money** to charity in the past month, adjusted for the country's GDP per capita.
 
• **Perceptions of Corruption**: This variable measures the **trust in institutions** by averaging responses on whether corruption is perceived as widespread in **government** and **business** sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Happiness Report (WHR) Context**:

 
 
• The report is published annually by the **United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**.
 
• The ranking is primarily based on the **Cantril Ladder**, where respondents rate their own current lives on a scale of 0 to 10.
 
• **Finland** has frequently secured the top position as the **happiest country** in the world for several consecutive years.
 
• The report includes a benchmark called **Dystopia**, an imaginary country with the world's least-happy people, used as a regression baseline.
 
• The first report was launched in **2012** to support the **UN High-Level Meeting** on well-being and happiness.

questions.question: When did India's men's national football team last qualify for the Olympic Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1960**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **India men's national football team** made its last appearance at the **Olympic Games** during the **1960 Rome Olympics**. Since then, the team has not been able to qualify for the final rounds of the tournament.
 
• In the **1960 Rome Olympics**, India was drawn into a highly challenging group, often referred to as the **Group of Death**, which included **Hungary**, **France**, and **Peru**.
 
• During this tournament, India delivered one of its most spirited performances by holding **France** to a **1-1 draw**, with the legendary **Tulsidas Balaram** scoring the equalizer.
 
• The team was led by **P.K. Banerjee** as the captain and coached by the visionary **Syed Abdul Rahim**, who is credited with the **Golden Era** of Indian football between **1951 and 1962**.
 
• Despite the draw against France, India lost to **Hungary (2-1)** and **Peru (3-1)**, leading to an early exit from the competition, marking the end of India's consistent presence on the world stage at the Olympics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1956 Melbourne Olympics**

 
 
• This was India's most successful Olympic campaign where they finished in **4th place**.
 
• **Neville D'Souza** became the first **Asian** to score a **hat-trick** in the Olympics during a 4-2 victory over **Australia**.
 
• India narrowly lost the bronze medal match to **Bulgaria** with a score of 3-0.
 
 
 
• **Other Olympic Appearances**
 
 
• India first participated in the **1948 London Olympics**, which was their first major international tournament as an independent nation. They played **barefoot** and lost 2-1 to **France**.
 
• The team also participated in the **1952 Helsinki Olympics** but suffered a heavy defeat against **Yugoslavia** in freezing conditions.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**
 
 
• The decline in Olympic qualification coincided with the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** and **FIFA** introducing age-restriction rules (U-23) for the tournament starting from **1992**.

questions.question: Which telescope provided the first direct image of a black hole?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Event Horizon Telescope**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Event Horizon Telescope (EHT)** is a large telescope array consisting of a global network of **radio telescopes** that are synchronized to function as a single, Earth-sized virtual observatory.
 
• On **April 10, 2019**, the EHT collaboration released the first-ever direct visual image of a **black hole** and its shadow, marking a historic milestone in astrophysics.
 
• The image depicts the supermassive black hole located at the center of **Messier 87 (M87)**, a massive galaxy in the **Virgo galaxy cluster**, situated approximately **55 million light-years** from Earth.
 
• This feat was accomplished using **Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI)**, a technique that allows researchers to observe celestial objects with incredibly high angular resolution by combining signals from multiple stations.
 
• The observation revealed a bright, ring-like structure caused by the bending of light in the intense gravity around the black hole, which has a mass **6.5 billion times** that of the Sun.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hubble Space Telescope**:

 
 
• Launched in **1990**, it orbits Earth and provides high-resolution images in **visible**, **ultraviolet**, and **near-infrared** light.
 
• While it has provided indirect evidence of black holes through stellar movement, it cannot resolve the **event horizon** directly.
 
 
 
• **Spitzer Space Telescope**:
 
 
• Launched in **2003** as part of **NASA**’s Great Observatories program, it specialized in **infrared astronomy**.
 
• It was used to study the **hidden regions** of the universe, such as dusty nebulae and the centers of galaxies, before being decommissioned in **2020**.
 
 
 
• **Kepler Space Telescope**:
 
 
• Launched in **2009**, its primary mission was to discover **Earth-sized planets** orbiting other stars.
 
• It used the **transit method** to identify over **2,700 confirmed exoplanets** during its operational lifetime.

questions.question: If an astronaut's mass is 70 kg, what will be their weight on the Moon (1/6th of Earth's gravity)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**117 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Mass** is an intrinsic property of matter that represents the amount of substance in an object and remains **constant** regardless of the gravitational environment; in this case, the astronaut's mass is **70 kg**.
 
• **Weight** is a measure of the **gravitational force** exerted on an object and is calculated using the formula Weight (W) = mass (m)

questions.question: Minimum Support Price (MSP) was introduced in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1960s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Minimum Support Price (MSP)** system was established in India during the **1960s** to stabilize agricultural prices and ensure **food security**.
 
• The **Agricultural Prices Commission (APC)** was constituted in **January 1965** to suggest appropriate price policies for agricultural commodities.
 
• The first **MSP** was declared by the Government of India for **Wheat** in the **1966-67** marketing season, following the recommendations of the **L.K. Jha Committee**.
 
• The policy was a key component of the **Green Revolution** strategy, intended to encourage farmers to adopt high-yielding varieties (**HYV**) and modern agricultural practices without fear of price crashes.
 
• It serves as a **floor price**, acting as a guarantee from the government to purchase crops at a fixed rate if market prices fall below the set threshold.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)**:

 
 
• In **March 1985**, the **Agricultural Prices Commission** was renamed the **Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)**.
 
• The **CACP** is a statutory body under the **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare** that recommends **MSP** for various crops based on production costs.
 
• The final decision on **MSP** levels is taken by the **Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA)**, which is chaired by the **Prime Minister**.
 
• Currently, the government announces **MSP** for **22 mandated crops**, including **14 Kharif crops**, **6 Rabi crops**, and **2 commercial crops** (Jute and Copra), along with the **Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP)** for **Sugarcane**.
 
• The price determination factors include **cost of production**, demand-supply balance, price trends in domestic and international markets, and terms of trade between agricultural and non-agricultural sectors.

questions.question: The Make in India initiative was launched in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Make in India** initiative was officially launched by the Prime Minister of India, **Narendra Modi**, on **September 25, 2014**, at **Vigyan Bhawan**, New Delhi.
 
• It is a major national program designed to facilitate investment, foster innovation, enhance skill development, protect **Intellectual Property**, and build best-in-class manufacturing infrastructure within the country.
 
• The initiative is spearheaded by the **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)**, which operates under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**.
 
• The primary objective of the program is to increase the manufacturing sector growth to **12−14%** per annum and to raise the sector's contribution to the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** from 16% to **25%** by **2025**.
 
• It aims to create **100 million** additional manufacturing jobs in the Indian economy by **2022** (later revised) to harness the country's demographic dividend.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Four Pillars of Make in India:**

 
 
• **New Processes:** Improving the **Ease of Doing Business** through deregulation and the introduction of the **e-Biz portal** for single-window clearances.
 
• **New Infrastructure:** Developing **Industrial Corridors**, **Smart Cities**, and integrating state-of-the-art technology to support logistics and supply chains.
 
• **New Sectors:** Opening up **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** in **25 focal sectors**, including significant liberalization in **Defense**, **Railways**, and **Space**.
 
• **New Mindset:** Changing the role of government from a regulator to a business facilitator.
 
 
 
• **Key Highlights:**
 
 
• The **Logo** of the initiative is a **striding lion** made of cogs, symbolizing manufacturing, strength, and national pride.
 
• The program promotes the **Zero Defect Zero Effect** slogan, which encourages high-quality manufacturing with zero environmental impact.
 
• Focal sectors include **Automobiles**, **Aviation**, **Biotechnology**, **Chemicals**, **Electronic Systems**, **Food Processing**, and **Renewable Energy**.

questions.question: Which micro-missile system did India test in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhargavastra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2025**, India successfully developed and tested **Bhargavastra**, an advanced **indigenous micro-missile system**.
 
• The system is specifically engineered to counter modern asymmetric threats, focusing on the destruction of **unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)**, low-flying aerial platforms, and light tactical ground assets.
 
• It incorporates high-end **miniaturized seeker technology** and precision-guided solid propulsion, ensuring high kill probability with a minimized collateral damage footprint.
 
• The **Bhargavastra** is highly versatile and capable of integration with **man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS)**, combat drones, and light utility vehicles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Astra-II**:

 
 
• It is a next-generation **Beyond-Visual-Range Air-to-Air Missile (BVRAAM)** developed indigenously by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**.
 
• It utilizes an advanced **dual-pulse solid rocket motor** to intercept highly maneuvering supersonic aerial targets at ranges exceeding **160 kilometers**.
 
 
 
• **Pralay**:
 
 
• It is a canisterized, **surface-to-surface short-range ballistic missile (SRBM)** developed for the tactical regiment of the **Indian Army**.
 
• It features a payload capacity of 350 kg to 1000 kg with an operational strike range of **150 to 500 kilometers**.
 
 
 
• **Vibhavasu**:
 
 
• Representing conceptual high-energy or thermal research parameters, it does not denote any active tactical micro-missile system in India's current weapon catalog.

questions.question: Which index measures wholesale prices?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wholesale Price Index**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Wholesale Price Index (WPI)** is a primary measure used to track the changes in the price of goods traded and sold in bulk by **wholesale businesses** to other businesses.
 
• In India, the **Office of Economic Adviser**, under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**, is responsible for compiling and releasing the WPI data on a monthly basis.
 
• The **base year** for the current WPI series in India is **2011-12**, which provides a benchmark for comparing price fluctuations over time.
 
• The index specifically tracks price movements at the **producer level** or the 'first point of sale', providing insights into the **inflationary pressures** within the production and manufacturing sectors.
 
• The WPI basket consists of three major commodity groups: **Manufactured Products** (which carries the highest weightage at 64.23%), **Primary Articles** (22.62%), and **Fuel and Power** (13.15%).
 
• Unlike other indices, the WPI only accounts for **goods** and does not include the price changes of **services**, making it a specialized tool for industrial and commercial price analysis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Consumer Price Index (CPI)**

 
 
• Measures the average change in prices paid by **retail consumers** for a basket of goods and services.
 
• It is released by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** and is the primary tool used by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** for **inflation targeting** and monetary policy.
 
 
 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP) Deflator**
 
 
• A comprehensive measure of inflation that reflects the prices of all **domestically produced** final goods and services in an economy.
 
• Calculated as the ratio of **Nominal GDP** to **Real GDP** multiplied by 100.
 
 
 
• **Index of Industrial Production (IIP)**
 
 
• An indicator that measures the **growth rate** in different industry groups of the economy in a fixed period.
 
• It tracks the **physical volume of production** rather than prices and is published by the **NSO** under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

questions.question: In _____, the Centre officially announced the scrapping of the 'No-Detention Policy' for Classes 5 and 8 in central government-run schools?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**December 2024**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Education** officially notified the scrapping of the **No-Detention Policy** for **Class 5** and **Class 8** in schools under the **Central Government** in **December 2024**.
 
• This move allows central government-run institutions, such as **Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs)** and **Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas (JNVs)**, to hold back students if they fail to clear the prescribed examinations.
 
• The decision is based on the **Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (Amendment) Act, 2019**, which modified the original **RTE Act of 2009** to give states and the Centre the power to decide on detention.
 
• According to the notification, students who fail the regular examination will be given **remedial coaching** and a opportunity for a **re-examination** within **two months** of the declaration of results.
 
• If a student fails the **re-examination**, the educational institution is now authorized to **detain** the child in the same grade to ensure they achieve the required **learning outcomes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **No-Detention Policy (NDP)**:

 
 
• Originally implemented under **Section 16** of the **RTE Act, 2009**, it mandated that no child be held back in any class until the completion of **elementary education** (up to Class 8).
 
• The primary objective was to reduce **school dropout rates** and eliminate the fear of failure among children aged **6 to 14 years**.
 
 
 
• **Reasons for Scrapping**:
 
 
• Several committees, including the **T.S.R. Subramanian Committee**, highlighted that the policy led to a lack of accountability and a significant decline in **academic standards** and **learning levels**.
 
• Data from the **National Achievement Survey (NAS)** indicated that many students in higher classes lacked basic **literacy and numeracy** skills.
 
 
 
• **Alignment with NEP 2020**:
 
 
• The **National Education Policy 2020** emphasizes a shift toward **competency-based learning** and regular assessment to track the progress of students effectively throughout their schooling.

questions.question: Who among the following was never the Nawab of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saadat Ali Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saadat Ali Khan I**, also known as **Burhan-ul-Mulk**, was the founder of the independent state of **Awadh** in **1722**. He served as the **Subahdar of Awadh** under the **Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah** and was never associated with the administration of **Bengal**.
 
• **Alivardi Khan** was the **Nawab of Bengal** from **1740 to 1756**. He was a strong ruler who seized power after defeating **Sarfaraz Khan** in the **Battle of Giria** and is noted for his successful military campaigns against the **Maratha** invaders.
 
• **Sirajuddaulah**, the grandson of **Alivardi Khan**, was the **Nawab of Bengal** from **1756 to 1757**. His reign is historically significant due to the **Battle of Plassey** in **June 1757**, where he was defeated by the **British East India Company** forces led by **Robert Clive**.
 
• **Mir Qasim** served as the **Nawab of Bengal** from **1760 to 1763**. He succeeded his father-in-law **Mir Jafar** with **British** support but later formed an alliance with the **Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II** and **Shuja-ud-Daula** of **Awadh** to fight the **British** in the **Battle of Buxar** in **1764**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nawabs of Bengal Dynasty**:

 
 
• **Murshid Quli Khan** (1717−1727) was the first independent **Nawab** who transferred the capital from **Dacca** to **Murshidabad**.
 
• The **Nawabi** rule effectively ended after the **Battle of Buxar**, leading to the **Treaty of Allahabad** in **1765**, which granted **Diwani Rights** to the **British**.
 
 
 
• **Nawabs of Awadh Dynasty**:
 
 
• **Saadat Ali Khan I** was responsible for establishing a semi-independent state as the **Mughal Empire** declined. He was succeeded by **Safdar Jung**.
 
• The **Awadh** rulers were known for their patronage of **Urdu** literature, architecture, and the distinct **Lucknowi** culture before the state was annexed in **1856**.

questions.question: Henry Lawrence was the Chief Commissioner of which state during the Revolt of 1857?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Awadh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sir Henry Lawrence** was a prominent British military officer and administrator who was appointed as the **Chief Commissioner of Awadh** (Oudh) in **March 1857**.
 
• He arrived in **Lucknow** just weeks before the outbreak of the **Great Revolt of 1857**, tasked with stabilizing the province after its controversial annexation by the British.
 
• Lawrence is best remembered for his leadership during the **Siege of Lucknow**; he anticipated the rebellion and moved the British population and loyal Indian troops into the fortified **Lucknow Residency**.
 
• His strategic foresight in stockpiling provisions and strengthening the defenses of the **Residency** complex is credited with the survival of the garrison during the prolonged siege.
 
• During the conflict, Lawrence was severely wounded by a fragment of an exploding shell on **July 2, 1857**, and succumbed to his injuries on **July 4, 1857**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Awadh (Oudh)**:

 
 
• The province was formally annexed by **Lord Dalhousie** in **1856** on the grounds of **maladministration** by the then-ruler, **Wajid Ali Shah**.
 
• This annexation caused widespread resentment among the **Taluqdars** and the **Bengal Army sepoys**, many of whom hailed from this region, making it a major center of the 1857 uprising.
 
 
 
• **Punjab**:
 
 
• Before his posting in Awadh, Henry Lawrence served as the President of the **Board of Administration** in **Punjab** following its annexation in **1849**.
 
• His brother, **John Lawrence**, was the Chief Commissioner of **Punjab** during the 1857 revolt and later became the **Viceroy of India**.
 
 
 
• **Odisha and Maharashtra**:
 
 
• While these regions saw localized disturbances, they were not the primary administrative focus of **Henry Lawrence** during the peak of the **1857 rebellion**.
